author: reek
body: The running process's state word says RUNNING. The scheduler's claim-before-publish protocol rests on that, and proc 0 is the one entry it is not true of by construction.

author: reek
body: A process becomes RUNNING by being claimed -- the claim is a CMPXCHG that moves the state word from READY to RUNNING, so every spawned process arrives in the right state on its own. Proc 0 is never spawned and never claimed: it is the program the machine booted, and its table entry is zeroed at boot along with the rest of the table. Zero is FREE. So it is initialised to RUNNING explicitly, and this test is what says so.

author: reek
body: Delete that initialisation and the failure is quiet and horrible. The timer's preemption publishes the process it interrupted as READY with a CMPXCHG from RUNNING -- which is a CMPXCHG precisely so that it cannot resurrect a process the max-ticks check has just zombified. If proc 0 sits at FREE, that compare never matches, proc 0 is never published, and the boot processor can never be scheduled back onto the program it was running. Nothing reports an error. The machine simply stops being the thing it was doing.
